deep.reconstruction:
This page is almost entirely drawings, made on the back of a recycled Cray‑2 job banner printout dated 16 Aug 1982. It continues the previous page, which deals with a configuration of pseudo-lines in the real projective plane. That page uses distinguished points s,t and u,u' and the cases III_{p,q} and I_n (the trivial case). It speaks of 'arcs de spécialisation' α, β of length 1/2 and of an 'exceptional specialization arc' γ, which has length 0 when only one pseudo-line avoids the distinguished points.

The drawings use the standard disk model of RP^2: a circle whose boundary is identified antipodally, i.e. the 'line at infinity'. Orange curves are pseudo-lines. Black (and green) boundary arcs mark the arcs of the line at infinity along which a degeneration/specialization takes place. The labels 1/2 are measured as fractions of the boundary (projective line) length.

- Top-right circle: several pseudo-lines; two short black marks at the ends of a horizontal diameter (the antipodal points u,u' or s,t); a long black arc along the bottom.
- Lower large circle: green and black boundary arcs with braces labelled 1/2, 1/2, 1/2. It shows a configuration where the specialization arcs have half-length.
- Small circle at bottom right: three marked boundary points labelled 1/2, 0, 1/2. This illustrates the degenerate case of the previous page, where the exceptional arc γ shrinks to a point (length 0) between two arcs of length 1/2.
- Horizontal strip diagram: an unrolled band, the boundary circle/Möbius band cut open. A black curve, partly dashed and partly doubled in green, passes from the upper edge to the lower edge through a crossing with the horizontal orange core line. Orange vertical and crossed pairs of oblique lines are pseudo-lines meeting the band. Hatching and small arrows suggest the moving of a curve (a deformation/specialization path) across crossings.

The overall aim appears to be classifying how a pseudo-line configuration can be specialized (points merging, lines passing through a vertex) as a parameter moves along the line at infinity. The aim is to measure, case by case, the length of the corresponding arcs. There is no text beyond the length labels, so the precise statement cannot be recovered from this page alone.
errors: Nothing checkable: the page contains no assertions beyond arc-length labels (1/2, 0), and these are consistent with the previous page's claim that γ has length 0 when there is a single pseudo-line avoiding the distinguished points.

The 'length' bookkeeping (1/2, 0) suggests a metric/combinatorial invariant of the degeneration strata that is not standard in the pseudoline literature. On its own, however, this page gives only illustrations.
